## Progress by stage

| Stage | Current evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Infrastructure | The gold-pipeline prototype uses Yahoo `GC=F` (COMEX continuous futures) and supports labeled local CSV input. A Stage 2 daily predictor panel downloads Yahoo DXY, S&P 500, and VIX observations plus FRED Treasury-yield, breakeven-inflation, and WTI series. An optional LSEG importer now builds a separate dataset from local Workspace exports, including `GCc1`, DXY, S&P 500, VIX, Treasury quotes, and gold-option quotes; this does not change the working Yahoo/FRED sources. Raw data and manifests remain Git-ignored. | Yahoo/FRED panel available; LSEG import is a partial alternative pending source-use, availability, and model-input review |
| Model development | Stage 1 used traditional univariate time-series methods on one gold-derived series. On the local prepared Yahoo `GC=F` snapshot through 2026-11-02, a rerun of the latest 500 requested origins produced 488 common forecasts (2024-11-07 to 2026-11-02): GARCH(1,1) fitting failed at 12 origins, which the comparison helper omits. GARCH(1,1) remained lowest in MAE/RMSE (0.000783/0.001891); its RMSE was 6.3% below expanding variance and 1.0% below EWMA. These differ slightly from the earlier 496-origin figures in the Stage 1 PDF and are exploratory point estimates, not a model decision. EGARCH(2,1) had the lowest in-sample AIC/BIC among 21 candidates, but 4 candidates did not converge and the current EGARCH setup does not include an asymmetry term. Stage 2's `notebooks/05_advanced_models.ipynb` screens the seven Yahoo/FRED candidates with training-only HAC coefficient t-tests; only VIX remains significant after Holm correction. A separate LSEG `GCc1` screen found DXY and VIX individually significant and the gold implied-volatility tenors jointly significant; those tenors are highly collinear, so individual tenor importance is unresolved. On the 596-origin Yahoo/FRED holdout, HistGradientBoosting RMSE (0.001883) exceeded the expanding-variance benchmark (0.001833). The Stage 3 comparison contains 20 models on 435 complete weekly origins from 445 requested dates (2018-01-05 to 2026-11-03), because GARCH(1,1) failed at 10 dates. HK selected ARIMA(3,1,1) using the first origin's history; its fixed order was refit successfully at all 445 origins. On the common sample its RMSE was 0.001048. GARCH(1,1) had the lowest point MSE, RMSE, and MAE; VAR had significantly larger MSE and QLIKE than historical variance after Holm correction. No candidate significantly beat historical variance. The older 500-origin GARCH(1,1) comparison is separate-sample context, not a same-origin benchmark. | Stage 1 and Stage 2 exploratory evidence available; Stage 3 aligned 20-model comparison complete; slow extensions deferred for runtime |
| Model analysis | EGARCH(2,1) residuals retained Ljung-Box autocorrelation at lag 20; squared standardized residuals did not show dependence at tested lags 10/20. Earlier full-sample HK runs selected conflicting orders; `docs/arima_discrepancy.md` records the uncertainty. The aligned evaluation instead fixes an order selected at its first origin, avoiding look-ahead. The Stage 3 comparison uses the five-session target and 435 shared usable origins from the 445 requested dates. No candidate beats the historical-variance benchmark after Holm correction; VAR's larger MSE and QLIKE are significantly different from the benchmark. The results do not settle a model choice. Extended-GARCH fits remain omitted from this runtime-limited comparison. | Samuel to review the Stage 3 loss, DM, and Mincer-Zarnowitz evidence; explain limitations and recommend a next step without assuming a selection criterion |

## Data readiness

- Keir selected gold futures as the Stage 2 working instrument; the current pipeline uses Yahoo Finance **`GC=F`**, a COMEX gold futures continuous series, not a single fixed-expiry contract. This does not settle a contract-specific strategy or license/redistribution rights.
- Yahoo Finance `XAUUSD=X` returned no data in the check recorded on 2026-11-06; `GC=F` was verified to return daily observations.
- The candidate panel uses Yahoo `DX-Y.NYB` (DXY), `^GSPC` (S&P 500 price index and derived close-to-close log return), `^VIX`, and `GC=F` volume when returned; FRED `DGS10`, `T10YIE`, and `DCOILWTICO`. FRED values are assigned a one-business-day availability proxy, not a series-specific release timestamp or historical vintage; Yahoo closes are aligned to the same date under the after-market-publication forecast origin.
- A separate LSEG import uses only `GCc1` for the gold target and assigns predictors to the next weekday after observation as an availability proxy. The current local export has no `ACVOL_1`, breakeven-inflation, or WTI file; LSEG spot/fixing requests failed. It produced 4,058 five-session forecast origins through 2026-11-03 and includes additional option-quote columns. This is a partial alternative dataset, not a replacement for the selected seven-variable panel or a model decision.
- Central-bank gold demand is deferred until a source and publication schedule support point-in-time alignment. Gold volume is optional and is a continuous-futures series measure, not a fixed-contract or exchange-wide volume measure.
- Raw downloads, prepared data, and manifests remain under Git-ignored `data/`. FRED series are downloaded as public CSVs without an API key. Check source-specific redistribution terms before committing any CSV; file size does not establish permission.
- The current prototype uses a five-observation forward realized-variance label by default; confirm the target definition and horizon before treating results as project decisions or fixing pipeline requirements.

## Git submissions by team member

The table and commit list below are generated from `git log --all` when this deck is rendered. With the main-only workflow, they show commits reachable from the locally available `main` history, attributed using the author identities mapped below. They do not count uncommitted changes or independently enumerate GitHub PRs. Fetch `main` before rendering so recent submissions appear.

```{python}
import subprocess

team_aliases = {
    "Keir": {"0keirli0", "keir"},
    "Enoch": {"enoch1uo", "enoch"},
    "Samuel": {"samuel"},
}

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        "git",
        "log",
        "--all",
        "--date=short",
        "--format=%h%x09%an%x09%ad%x09%s",
    ],
    check=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)

commits = []
for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
    commit_hash, author, commit_date, subject = line.split("\t", maxsplit=3)
    normalized_author = author.strip().casefold()
    member = next(
        (
            name
            for name, aliases in team_aliases.items()
            if normalized_author in aliases
        ),
        author,
    )
    commits.append(
        {
            "Member / author": member,
            "Commit": commit_hash,
            "Date": commit_date,
            "Submission": subject,
        }
    )

if not commits:
    print("No commits are visible in the current repository refs.")
else:
    counts = {member: 0 for member in team_aliases}
    latest = {member: "—" for member in team_aliases}
    for commit in commits:
        member = commit["Member / author"]
        if member in counts:
            counts[member] += 1
            if latest[member] == "—":
                latest[member] = f'{commit["Date"]} ({commit["Commit"]})'

    print("| Member | Visible commits | Latest visible commit |")
    print("|---|---:|---|")
    for member in team_aliases:
        print(f"| {member} | {counts[member]} | {latest[member]} |")

    print("\nRecent submissions visible in Git history:")
    print("| Author | Commit | Date | Submission |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|")
    for commit in commits[:12]:
        subject = commit["Submission"].replace("|", "\\|")
        print(
            f'| {commit["Member / author"]} | {commit["Commit"]} '
            f'| {commit["Date"]} | {subject} |'
        )
```

Before rendering, fetch the shared `main` branch so the report includes its latest commits:
